name: Code Review Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on code review so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on code review so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about code review explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Prefer explicit, readable code review solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to code review (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. Validate code review outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. When code review guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Prefer the simplest code review approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. When multiple code review strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop code review edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic code review advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new code review abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated code review concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting code review assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for code review, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
